# Finding the PDF of $\frac{X_1}{X_1+X_2+X_3}$ for $n=3$

## Setting Up the Problem

Since $X_1 + X_2 + X_3 = 1$ by constraint, the ratio simplifies:

$$\frac{X_1}{X_1 + X_2 + X_3} = \frac{X_1}{1} = X_1$$

So I need the **marginal PDF of $X_1$** when $(X_1, X_2, X_3)$ are **jointly uniform** over the simplex:
$$S = \{(x_1, x_2, x_3) : x_i \geq 0,\; x_1 + x_2 + x_3 = 1\}$$

## Finding the Joint PDF

Since $x_3 = 1 - x_1 - x_2$, the feasible region in the $(x_1, x_2)$-plane is the triangle with vertices $(0,0)$, $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$, which has area $\frac{1}{2}$.

The joint PDF is constant over this region:

$$f_{X_1,X_2}(x_1, x_2) = \frac{1}{\text{Area}} = \frac{1}{1/2} = 2, \quad \text{for } x_1 \geq 0,\; x_2 \geq 0,\; x_1 + x_2 \leq 1$$

## Computing the Marginal PDF of $X_1$

Integrate out $x_2$:

$$f_{X_1}(x_1) = \int_{0}^{1-x_1} 2 \, dx_2 = 2(1 - x_1), \quad 0 \leq x_1 \leq 1$$

## Verification

$$\int_0^1 2(1-x)\,dx = 2\left[x - \frac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^1 = 2\left(1 - \tfrac{1}{2}\right) = 1 \;\checkmark$$

## Result

The ratio $Y = \dfrac{X_1}{X_1+X_2+X_3} = X_1$ follows a **Beta(1, 2)** distribution with PDF:

$$f_Y(y) = \begin{cases} 2(1-y) & 0 \leq y \leq 1 \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$

This is a decreasing linear density, reflecting that smaller values of $X_1$ (relative to the whole) are more probable than larger values on the simplex.

$$\boxed{2(1-x)}, \quad 0 \le x \le 1$$
